answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it can submit work or claim rewards. When independent reviewers verify a task, they release payment for valid work and slash stake for proven fraud; creating more identities does not multiply the attacker's influence without also tying up more capital. The opal, lagoon, and timber markets can each set their own minimum stake, making a Sybil campaign costly across distinct tasks rather than free through account creation.
